transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in today?

Well, it's really hard for me to admit this, but when I’m stressed after work and classes, I end up eating way more food in one sitting than seems normal for anyone. It's just gotten to the point where it feels completely out of hand, and I knew I needed to talk to someone about it.
After these episodes of eating a very large amount of food, do you ever try to make up for it by vomiting, using laxatives, fasting, or exercising excessively? If so, which of these do you do?

No, I don't do any of those things like throwing up, taking laxatives, or trying to exercise it off. After it happens, I just feel incredibly full, exhausted, and ashamed, so I usually just lie down or go to bed. I've never tried to "undo" it in those ways.
How often do these episodes happen, and for how many months have they been going on? During them, does it feel like you can’t stop or control how much you’re eating?

This has been happening at least once a week—often more—for about four months now. When it's happening, I feel completely out of control, like my brain switches off and my hand is on autopilot reaching for food even when I'm telling myself to stop.

During these episodes, do you also eat much more quickly than usual, eat until you feel uncomfortably full, eat when you’re not physically hungry, or eat alone because you feel embarrassed? Which of these happens to you?

I definitely eat until I’m painfully full and bloated, and most of the time I'm not even physically hungry when I start. I also hide in my room to eat alone because I feel so embarrassed about how much I'm putting away. I'm not really sure if I eat faster than usual, but those other three things definitely happen to me.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports recurrent binge-eating episodes at least weekly for 4 months, with a clear sense of loss of control, marked distress/shame, and associated features including eating until uncomfortably full, eating when not hungry, and eating alone due to embarrassment. There are no compensatory behaviors such as vomiting, laxative use, fasting, or excessive exercise. This pattern is most consistent with binge-eating disorder, classified in ICD-10 under other eating disorders.
